covalent attachment of luminescent nanocrystals via cysteine residues to the membrane-integrated Fo1F1 ATP synthase leads to a significant reduction of the blinking probability of the nanocrystals, which allows the observation of the rotation of the rotor subunit in the time range from microseconds to seconds.
covalently linked CdSe/ZnSe quantum dots can be used to study the subunit rotation of FoF1 in the presence of the lipid bilayer.

the covalent binding to the FoF1 subunit c of a hydrophilic CdSe/Zn S QD with a hydrophilized shell leads to the reduction of the QD blinking probability and to the detection of the subunit rotation of FoF1 in an extended time window.

the development of a new class of luminescent probes for single-pair FRET studies.
the development of novel methods for the investigation of single molecules and the use of luminescent QDs for this purpose.
the development of novel QD-based single-molecule techniques for studying the function and dynamics of membrane- integrated proteins.

the QD is not only useful for long-term single-pair measurements but also for the investigation of the dynamics of subunit rotation in FoF1.
